# The no-opener two-root renderer kill has no committed witness

## Context

#18376 measures a renderer kill: a second root of a canvas-drawing SharedWorker app, opened with **no opener**, terminates the first root's renderer process. It has been measured three times — 2026-09-05, 2026-09-12 and 2026-09-15 — and **not once from a spec that lives in this repository.** #18376's own body records the cost: *"The 2026-09-05 probe was written outside the tree and is gone."*

Its AC-1 asks for exactly this witness. This leaf delivers that one criterion so it can land independently of the fix, which is #18376's AC-2 through AC-6 and now has a folded shape ([D#18730](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/18730), `[GRADUATION_APPROVED]` by @neo-gpt, 2026-09-21).

## The Problem

A defect whose only evidence is prose in a ticket body cannot red when someone reintroduces it, cannot green when someone fixes it, and is re-derived from scratch by every session that touches the area. Three separate measurements produced no artifact.

**And #18376's AC-1 as written cannot be CI-gated.** It specifies *"two full Workstation roots"*, and `test/playwright/e2e/workstation` is a declared GPU exclusion in `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs` — *"specs booting the workstation app, which inherits animated OffscreenCanvas work no hosted runner can composite."* Every workstation spec is also a Neural Link spec, deselected by `playwright.config.e2e.mjs`'s `testIgnore` without `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT`. A Workstation witness would run on no CI job and report `Skipped: 0` while doing so.

**Measured 2026-09-21 at `a29a2e3935`: it does not need Workstation.** `apps/portal` declares `useCanvasWorker: true` and `useSharedWorkers: true` and draws canvases, which is the affected configuration #18376 names. Three arms, 21.4 s total, one worker:

| arm | root B | root A after 8 s |
|---|---|---|
| control | none | alive, 9 canvases |
| control | `window.open` (opener, shares the renderer process) | alive, 9 canvases; B alive too |
| red | `context.newPage()` (no opener, own process) | **`Page crashed`** |

Both controls pass and only the red arm dies, so the arm witnesses the **process boundary** rather than "something went wrong while a second root booted".

## The Architectural Reality

- `apps/portal/neo-config.json` — `useCanvasWorker: true`, `useSharedWorkers: true`; four canvas consumers (`view/home/FooterCanvas.mjs`, `view/home/parts/hero/Canvas.mjs`, `view/content/TimelineCanvas.mjs`, `view/services/Canvas.mjs`).
- `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs` — `RUN_PATHS` includes `test/playwright/e2e/core` and `test/playwright/e2e/portal`; `assertSelectionFloor` fails the job if the executed population shrinks, so a new spec inside those roots is genuinely executed rather than silently deselected.
- `test/playwright/e2e/core/SharedWorkerRemoteReplay.spec.mjs` — the existing sibling for engine-level SharedWorker behaviour across two windows, and the dialect this spec follows (`context.newPage()`, `watch(page)` problem collection, readiness by value rather than by clock).
- `src/component/Canvas.mjs:87-102` — the single inward transfer every canvas component inherits, via `Neo.main.DomAccess.transferCanvasToWorker` (`src/main/DomAccess.mjs:1419`). The trigger #18376 isolated is root B's OffscreenCanvases, and this is the only path that produces them.

## The Fix

One spec, `test/playwright/e2e/core/` — engine-level shared-worker behaviour, beside `SharedWorkerRemoteReplay.spec.mjs`, not under `portal/` where the app is only the vehicle.

Three arms, in this order:

1. **control — root A alone.** Boots `apps/portal`, asserts `useSharedWorkers`, `useCanvasWorker` and a non-zero canvas count, then stays alive across the same wall-clock window the red arm dies in.
2. **control — an opener root.** `window.open` from root A. Both roots alive.
3. **red — a no-opener root.** `context.newPage()` + `goto`. Root A dies.

Arm 3 carries `test.fail()`: the suite is green while #18376 is open, and the arm reds the moment the defect is fixed — which is the signal to delete that line. Arms 1 and 2 are the controls that make arm 3 mean something: they boot identically, so a broken boot or a fragile root A reds them rather than quietly satisfying the expected failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 — The spec lives at `test/playwright/e2e/core/`, inside `RUN_PATHS`, and needs neither `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` nor a GPU.
- [ ] AC-2 — Three arms as above. Both controls pass on `dev`; the red arm fails on `dev` and is marked `test.fail()`, so the suite reports green.
- [ ] AC-3 — Mutation-checked: with the red arm's `test.fail()` removed it reds, and with root B's launch changed from `context.newPage()` to `window.open` it passes. Both results recorded in the PR.
- [ ] AC-4 — The docblock names what the arm witnesses (a second renderer process painting through the shared canvas worker), links #18376, and states the one limit honestly: `test.fail()` accepts *any* failure, so the two controls — not the red arm — are what rule out an unrelated cause.
- [ ] AC-5 — `node buildScripts/util/check-fixed-sleeps.mjs` reports `0 new`. The settle waits are wall-clock under test and carry the `wall-clock-under-test:` marker.

## Out of Scope

- **The fix.** #18376's AC-2 through AC-6 — the presenter contract, the cost criterion, the Workstation arm, the engine matrix.
- **The heap boundary.** D#18730's B/D/E/F, Group identity, worker discovery, the reconnect lease and Neural Link routing all stay open and are untouched by a test.
- **A Workstation arm.** It stays #18376's AC-3, where it belongs, and remains local/dispatch-only for the GPU reason above.

## Avoided Traps

- **A permanently red spec.** Committing the red arm unmarked would red `dev` for every PR until the fix lands, which trains everyone to ignore it. `test.fail()` inverts it: green while broken, red when fixed.
- **A witness that witnesses nothing.** `test.fail()` is satisfied by *any* failure, including a broken boot. That is why arms 1 and 2 exist and must pass; without them the red arm would keep passing after `apps/portal` stopped booting at all.
- **Following AC-1's wording literally.** *"Two full Workstation roots"* was written before the GPU exclusion was relevant to it. Taken at face value it produces a spec no CI job runs — the `Skipped: 0` failure mode `e2eCiSelection.mjs`'s own docblock warns about.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — a witness for an existing defect. The shape it will eventually witness green is [D#18730](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/18730)'s narrow G, which preserves ADR 0029's worker-truth / per-window render-target boundary rather than amending it.
